comments.body:
Phase 1 confirmed RCA (before repair):

The defect is test isolation, not production auth validation. `tests/unit/test_rp04_s4_llm_runtime_heldout.py:41`, `:60`, and `:125` replace the SDK class `anthropic.AsyncAnthropic` with ordinary functions before the lazily loaded `pydantic_ai.providers.anthropic` module is present. On first import, pydantic-ai 1.107.2 captures the patched function and evaluates its runtime `AsyncAnthropic | AsyncAnthropicBedrock | ...` TypeAlias at installed provider lines 34-36, producing `TypeError: unsupported operand type(s) for |: function and type` before rebar reaches `anthropic_auth_kwargs` (`src/rebar/llm/anthropic_model.py:107-119`). `sys.modules` explains the order sensitivity.

Discriminating runtime proof on current main 0f7461d243: each of the three function-patched held-out nodes fails in a fresh Python 3.12.13 process at the union; each passes when the provider is pre-imported. Replacing AsyncAnthropic with a class-shaped double in a fresh process reaches the contractually required secret-free `LLMConfigError`, with constructor count 0. The class-preserving/pre-imported controls pass: `test_only_selected_provider_carrier_consumed`, `test_anthropic_api_key_reaches_the_client`, and `test_construction_guard_fails_fast_on_nonzero_sdk_retries`. A meta-path import blocker observed `events=[provider-import]` and no validation event, proving imports currently precede validation, while an unblocked real-SDK run imports the provider and then raises the correct secret-free LLMConfigError. That ordering is a contributing seam but not an independently authorized production defect: the cited contract at the held-out module lines 3-7, the target nodes, `anthropic_model.py:100-105`, and `auth.py:71-78` promises failure before client construction/request, not before dependency import.

Legitimacy: defect. The existing oracle explicitly requires a typed LLMConfigError and secret-free error message; its function-shaped test double prevents the production behavior from being exercised. Minimal repair target: preserve the SDK symbol’s class contract in all three live sibling patches. No production source change is warranted.

comments.body:
Final rebar-debug report (unpublished commit 4dc4ca87559ef213c04dec7cc8fd282293a6366b):

Problem — three Anthropic auth held-out tests could fail or pass solely according to prior provider-import order.

Proven root cause — `tests/unit/test_rp04_s4_llm_runtime_heldout.py` replaced the SDK class `anthropic.AsyncAnthropic` with functions at the three invalid-auth sites. A first lazy import of pydantic-ai 1.107.2 captures that function and evaluates it in `AsyncAnthropic | AsyncAnthropicBedrock | ...`, raising a dependency import TypeError before rebar auth validation. The test-double representation is the changeable defect; production validation-before-client/request semantics are correct.

Proof — fresh-process plain/pre-import/class-double matrix: all three function-shaped nodes failed at the runtime union with the provider absent; provider pre-import made each pass; a class-shaped double reached the expected secret-free LLMConfigError with constructor count 0. A meta-path blocker observed provider import before validation, but a normal real-SDK run still produced the intended secret-free LLMConfigError. Class-shaped/pre-imported controls all passed.

Test — added `tests/unit/test_anthropic_lazy_import_isolation_heldout.py`, which starts a child interpreter, asserts the provider is absent from `sys.modules`, and runs each of the three affected nodes plus a class-preserving negative control. Final oracle was observed RED first (3 failed, 1 passed), then GREEN (4 passed) after the held-out fixer. Reintroducing the exact function-shaped patch made the affected parameter RED with the same union TypeError; restoring the fix returned the relevant set to GREEN. The oracle asserts child-process exit/real target behavior, not private source shape, and process exit retires all import state.

Fix — changed the three AsyncAnthropic doubles to classes whose constructors retain the existing fail-if-constructed tripwires. This preserves the SDK symbol contract without pre-importing the provider to mask the issue. No production source changed.

Scope and safety — callers are confined to these test-local monkeypatch sites; all other uses are incidental controls. The change restores intended tests, adds no dependency/capability, and weakens no assertion. Pytest still automatically restores each attribute patch.

Siblings — construct sweep covered every AsyncAnthropic patch plus SDK/provider-class monkeypatch candidates. Fixed all three live function-before-lazy-import siblings in the held-out module. Benign controls: the same module’s selected-provider case pre-imports the provider and uses a class; `test_rp04_s4_llm_runtime.py` pre-imports and uses a class; `test_transport_retry.py` uses a class; OpenAI/Bedrock tests patch already-imported provider symbols/classes. Parity axis is N/A: this is a test-double representation rule, not a multi-channel product operation.

Verification — after rebase onto origin/main 4c3e5970e6: focused Anthropic/auth/retry set 31 passed; `make lint` passed; `make typecheck` passed; commit-ticket verification passed; worktree clean. The supported full run reached 13,990 passed / 62 skipped and all Anthropic targets passed; its sole failure was the unrelated live-Jira index visibility defect `dutiable-shaded-honeyeater` (`test_delete_permission_probe`, REB-3162), already open with multiple identical reproductions, so it was not retried or duplicated.

Residual risk and prevention — live Jira visibility flake is dispositioned to existing bug `dutiable-shaded-honeyeater`. No residual Anthropic import-order fragility remained in the bounded test sweep.

Replication — the originally failing conflict-error node and both siblings now pass individually in fresh provider-absent interpreters; the full supported run no longer reproduces this defect.

## Context / Problem
A supported full-suite run can fail in `tests/unit/test_rp04_s4_llm_runtime_heldout.py::test_secret_absent_from_conflict_error_message` when the test replaces `anthropic.AsyncAnthropic` with a lambda before `pydantic_ai.providers.anthropic` is first imported. The dependency constructs an import-time union containing that attribute and raises `TypeError: unsupported operand type(s) for |: function and type`. Determine whether this is a production defect or order-dependent test isolation, and sweep sibling monkeypatch-before-lazy-import cases.

## Investigation and repair plan
- Reproduce the failure on current `origin/main` both in the polluted lazy-import order and in an isolated control order.
- Trace the runtime import path and test seam, inspect history and adjacent tests, and prove one falsifiable root cause before repair.
- Cite the intended test contract and classify production versus test-isolation ownership.
- Inventory existing coverage and create or strengthen the smallest in-process oracle that forces the lazy-import state and asserts the secret-redaction contract still reaches its intended conflict error.
- Apply the minimal remediation at the owned seam, then prove RED to GREEN, exact-defect mutation sensitivity, original-report replication, and sibling coverage.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Runtime evidence proves the import-order mechanism and distinguishes it from production secret-redaction behavior.
- [ ] The in-process unit oracle forces a fresh Anthropic provider import after the monkeypatch and observes the contractual redacted conflict error rather than a dependency import `TypeError`.
- [ ] The oracle is observed RED before repair, GREEN after repair, and RED again under an exact-defect mutation.
- [ ] A bounded sweep identifies and disposes every sibling test that replaces an SDK runtime class before the corresponding pydantic-ai provider module is imported.
- [ ] The original failing node and its supported relevant suite pass in both isolated and order-sensitive execution.
- [ ] The ticket records the final RCA, caller/safety assessment, sibling disposition, and replication evidence.
